name: Colored sunglasses lenses
lead: Colored sunglasses lenses are tinted lenses, such as yellow, orange, rose or blue, worn mainly for style in looksmaxxing and fashion contexts. A tint changes the colour of the wearer's view and, depending on the colour, can alter contrast and colour discrimination.[1][2]
Published research on tinted lenses is about vision and medical symptoms (contrast, light sensitivity, migraine, blepharospasm), not about how they change facial attractiveness.

paras: A laboratory study of 20 young subjects compared clear lenses with yellow, dark yellow and orange lenses and linked the contrast enhancement of yellow lenses to selective reduction of short-wavelength light.[1] A later study reported that tinted lenses enhanced contrast sensitivity while causing losses of chromatic discrimination.[2] A literature review examined whether tinted lenses or filters improve visual performance in low vision.[3]

FL-41 tinted lenses were tested in randomised crossover studies of benign essential blepharospasm, where they were compared with gray lenses for blink frequency and light sensitivity.[4] Tinted spectacles have also been studied in visually sensitive migraine.[5] Interventions that reduce evening blue-light exposure were reviewed in a meta-analysis for effects on sleep.[6]
The entry was added as a style item. No forum material on it was available, so community claims are not documented here.
No studies found on coloured sunglasses and facial appearance. Studies of tinted lenses exist for contrast, light sensitivity and migraine, as described above.[1][2][4][5]

card.summary: Tinted sunglasses are a style choice; research covers contrast and light sensitivity, not looks.
card.note: Tints can reduce colour discrimination, per optometry studies.

quick.overview:
Colored sunglasses lenses are tinted eyewear chosen for style. The tint changes how the wearer sees colour and contrast.

No study found tests whether they change how attractive a face looks. Existing research covers vision and medical light sensitivity.
quick.mechanism: Tinted lenses filter parts of the light spectrum. Yellow and orange filters reduce short-wavelength light, which a study linked to higher contrast, with some loss of colour discrimination.
quick.risks: Studies note reduced colour discrimination with some tints. The sources reviewed document no other harms.
